findings.title: Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (the "nothing" case is `NOTHING_CONDITION`, not null), so `authConditions` is always truthy. The `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches (lines 76-80) can never run. Simplify to: `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` : authConditions;`. The dead fallback also suggests an auth-less path exists when it does not.

findings.title: Unparenthesized OR returned from getFilterConditions
findings.body: With only `eventTypeId` set, `getFilterConditions()` returns `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` with no outer parentheses. It is safe today because `getBaseConditions` and the AND-reduce wrap each operand in parentheses, and `getBaseConditions` has no other caller in the repo. But `getFilterConditions` is public, and a caller who ANDs its result without wrapping would silently change precedence and leak rows outside the filter. Wrap the OR in its own parentheses: `Prisma.sql`((("eventTypeId" = ${id}) OR ("eventParentId" = ${id})))``. The test at the `getFilterConditions` eventTypeId case would need the same update.

findings.title: Caching tests removed although caching still exists; getBaseConditions has a single case
findings.body: The `Caching` describe block was deleted, but `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` still exist in `insightsBooking.ts` (lines 49-50, 83-95). The old tests were weak (they compared two equal values), but the cache is no longer covered at all. `getBaseConditions` is also tested only for the owner + filter case. There is no test that a non-admin user gets `1=0` through the raw query and returns zero rows, or that the no-filter path returns the auth condition alone. The raw-SQL path is the only one that exercises Postgres's handling of `ANY(${array})` parameters and the parenthesization, so one more query-level test for the org/team scopes would be worthwhile.

findings.title: Public options type duplicates the zod schema and loosens type safety
findings.body: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` allows `{scope: "team"}` without `teamId`, which the zod schema rejects. That case is now caught only at runtime, where it silently becomes `options = null` and the authorization condition falls back to `1=0`. The compiler no longer flags a missing `teamId`. If the goal was to avoid exposing the zod-inferred type, a discriminated TS union that mirrors the schema would keep the compile-time check.

contracts.action: Replace Prisma findMany-based authorization/filter conditions with raw Prisma.sql fragments consumed through $queryRaw
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous `findMany` on `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized` (removed) combined auth and filter WhereInputs with AND.
contracts.before_after: Before: `findMany` merged `{AND:[auth, filter]}` with the caller's where. After: `getBaseConditions` returns `(auth) AND (filter)` as Sql, and the caller embeds it in its own query. The authorization-first semantics are kept: auth is always included and denies by default with `1=0`. No in-repo caller of `findMany` or `getBaseConditions` exists besides the test.
contracts.visible_effect: No UI path yet. The service has no callers outside its integration test.
contracts.failure_mode: Invalid or non-admin options give `1=0`, so no rows are returned and nothing throws. Team scope with an unknown team gives `1=0`. Empty member lists are handled by skipping the userId clause. Only operator precedence could leak rows, and every combination site wraps its operands in parentheses.

summary: The raw-SQL conversion of InsightsBookingService looks correct. Authorization is always applied and defaults to `1=0`. Operands are parenthesized at every combination site, and empty user lists are handled. I found only minor points: dead branches in `getBaseConditions`, an unwrapped OR returned from the public `getFilterConditions`, the removed caching tests and thin `getBaseConditions` coverage, and a looser public options type.
